primitives.name: Brier Skill Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: Implement Brier Skill Score (BSS) relative to base rate: BSS = 1 - BS/BS_ref, BS_ref = base_rate * (1 - base_rate).
primitives.assumptions: Binary outcome space; base rate remains fixed over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model predicts constant probability, BSS becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: BSS provides normalized measure of forecast accuracy against baseline performance.
layer2.telemetry: Model performance relative to naive predictor.

primitives.name: Expected Calibration Error Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Gate passes only if observed ECE <= null_q95 + tolerance.
primitives.assumptions: Null model has known quantile threshold; tolerance is bounded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when ECE exceeds critical value under null hypothesis.

layer2.mapping: ECE gate enforces statistical consistency between predicted and actual outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Observed calibration error compared to null model.

primitives.name: Tail Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Tail calibration: reliability for p > 0.7, 0.3-0.7, p < 0.3.
primitives.assumptions: Probability bins are disjoint and cover support of p.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Poor reliability in extreme probability regions.

layer2.mapping: Tail calibration ensures forecast validity across high and low probability regimes.

The three primitives—BSS, ECE gate, and tail calibration—are foundational for constructing robust probabilistic forecasts. BSS normalizes forecast skill against a base-rate benchmark, ensuring that improvements over naive guessing are meaningful. The ECE gate acts as a statistical filter, enforcing that models meet minimum calibration standards before deployment. Tail calibration further refines this by checking reliability in extreme probability zones where misprediction can be most costly. Together, they define a calibration triad that supports both internal rigor and external interpretability. Failure modes include overfitting to training data, ignoring tail behavior, or relaxing thresholds without sufficient justification. These primitives also enable dualities such as the equivalence between BSS and Brier score under certain assumptions, and the relationship between ECE and expected loss in proper scoring rules.
